correctness.rationale: For symmetric continuous-time rates on a tree, solving the target Dirichlet problem yields E_u τ_v=Σ_{e on path} size(source-side component of T\e)/w_e. Maximal ordered pairs may be chosen among leaves. Averaging within the two leaf classes gives four reciprocal-rate candidate maxima: Nx, Ny, x+(N-1)y+(m+1)z, (N-1)x+y+(m+1)z. For arbitrary unequal individual rates those averages are universal lower bounds; positive convex combinations and Cauchy–Schwarz give exact dual lower certificates and force all edges in each class equal at equality. Optimizers yield H1=(N-1)L, H2=(N-1)(sqrt(mL)+sqrt(R(m+1)))²/m; below H1 equal spokes, in (H1,H2) directed cheap-to-expensive crossing, above H2 within-expensive and crossing tie. Unique global optimization follows strict positive dual coefficients and budget saturation, with boundary continuity. Independent exact CTMC solve for m=2 and rational edge rates and direct numerical 3-phase tests (H=5,10,30; L=1,R=2/3) corroborate the analytic certificates. The limit m>=2 is essential for within-class leaf pairs.

The two price thresholds distinguish equal-spoke, directed-crossing, and within-class tradeoffs that resistance diameter cannot capture.
